quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do if you ride on a slippery surface?

options.text: Slow down
Speed up
Make sudden moves

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed and avoid sudden moves. Use both brakes carefully.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You will have more escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver cannot see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Which part of the lane is safest?

options.text: Always the left side
Always the right side
It depends on the situation

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always safest. Change your position based on the current conditions and what is happening around you.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, just like car mirrors
No, they do not
Mirrors are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, just like car mirrors
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more distance ahead
Ignore them
Speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more distance ahead
questions.explanation: Ride in a way that encourages the tailgater to pass you. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes
Proceed with caution
Turn around and find another route

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes
questions.explanation: Come to a complete stop at a flashing railroad crossing sign. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you proceed. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: What should you do after riding over an object on the road?

options.text: Keep riding because the danger is gone
Pull over and check your tires and rims for damage
Stop to remove the object from the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check your tires and rims for damage
questions.explanation: Pull off the road and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is caught in your drive chain or belt before riding further.

questions.question: What should you do when you see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle
Wait until the vehicle starts moving again
Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the emergency vehicle extra space and proceed with caution. Slow down and be ready to stop when approaching an emergency scene.

questions.question: How does one alcoholic drink affect your ability to ride?

options.text: You cannot be convicted of DUI
It will not affect your riding skills
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle
questions.explanation: Your ability to ride safely is affected after just one drink. You can be convicted of riding impaired even if your blood alcohol is below the legal limit.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of the lane behind a car, what is the main problem?

options.text: Drivers do not check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror
Wind may prevent the use of side mirrors
Drivers should not use side mirrors

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers do not check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver will see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: You should pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you more visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
You like, without thinking about other riders.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you more visible and gives you safe space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you best and where you have space around your motorcycle. There is no single best lane position for all situations. Good riders change their position as road conditions change.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen in daylight, you:

options.text: Do not need to wear bright clothing during the day.
Should wear bright clothing during the day.
Should wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear bright clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight hours. Wear bright clothing when you ride, even during the day. This helps other drivers notice you.

questions.question: It can be difficult to ride right after it starts raining because:

options.text: Some drivers may not react fast enough to the rain.
The road becomes very slippery.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes very slippery.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the road becomes very slippery. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away, so it mixes with the water and creates a slippery surface.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: What should be your first consideration when buying a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: Appearance
Protection
Price

questions.correctAnswerText: Protection
questions.explanation: Protection should come first when buying a helmet. Choose a helmet that fits snugly, fastens securely, and meets DOT safety standards.

questions.question: When traveling at night, it is:

options.text: Easier to judge distances than during the day.
About as easy to judge distances as during the day.
Harder to judge distances than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder to judge distances than during the day.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge how far away objects are. Light and shadows help you judge distance during the day. At night, artificial lights may distort or hide these helpful clues.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Sneakers
Leather boots
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots offer the best protection for motorcycle riders. Choose boots that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:

options.text: Leather.
Wool.
Any soft material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Leather gloves give you the best grip and protection. Choose leather or similar durable materials for riding gloves.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Are nothing to worry about.
Should be checked regularly by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked regularly by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is not dangerous.
Can cause permanent hearing damage.
Is just part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind noise from riding can permanently damage your hearing over time. Wear ear protection when you ride. Good ear protection will protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes because it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you.
Wear shorts if it is hot, whatever is comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright clothes at all times so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Not use turn signals.
Position your motorcycle properly in your lane.
Follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle properly in your lane.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, be visible, signal your moves, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not change gears.
Shift up through the gears.
Shift down through the gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes.
Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work properly.
Check that the paint on your bike is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test both brake controls to make sure each one lights up your brake lights.
